ko.title: [Consumer Psychology #15] 팔리게 하는 같은 기술이 발목을 잡을 수도 있다: 윤리, 웰빙, 그리고 전체 강의 요약

segments.src: > The psychology that makes marketing work, like attention, memory, and mental shortcuts, can help people choose well or push them into choices they regret. Ethics comes down to which of those two things a design is doing.
segments.tr: > 마케팅을 작동하게 하는 심리, 즉 주의, 기억, 정신적 지름길은 사람이 현명하게 선택하도록 도울 수도 있고, 후회할 선택으로 밀어붙일 수도 있습니다. 윤리의 문제는 어떤 설계가 둘 중 어느 쪽을 하고 있느냐에 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 이 시리즈에서 우리는 소비자가 사물을 알아차리고, 기억하고, 태도를 형성하고, 사회적 압력에 굴복하고, 정신적 지름길을 택하는 방식을 살펴봤습니다.

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: 핵심만 짧게 정리하면 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **지각과 주의:** 우리는 주변의 일부만 알아차리기 때문에, 대비, 움직임, 새로움이 주의를 끕니다.

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **기억:** 여러 번 본 브랜드는 익숙하게 느껴지고, 익숙한 것은 안전하게 느껴지는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **태도와 설득:** 관심이 있고 시간이 있을 때는 강력한 논거에 설득됩니다. 주의가 흩어져 있을 때는 유명인, 귀에 맴도는 징글, 큰 숫자 같은 표면적 단서가 설득의 역할을 합니다.

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **사회적 영향:** 리뷰, "베스트셀러" 배지, 친구들이 사는 물건은 무엇이 '보통'인지를 알려 줍니다.

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **결정 지름길(휴리스틱):** 앵커링, 손실 회피, 기본값, 희소성은 우리가 빠르게 결정하도록 돕지만, 쉽게 악용되기도 합니다.

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: 이 도구들은 모두 두 가지 방식으로 쓰일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: 가격을 비교하도록 돕는 명확한 표시는 주의를 정직하게 활용합니다.

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: 페이지를 새로 고칠 때마다 다시 시작되는 카운트다운 타이머는 같은 도구를 써서 사용자를 속입니다.

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: 디자인이 사용자 자신의 이익에 의도적으로 반하도록 작동할 때, 이를 **다크 패턴**이라고 합니다.

segments.src: In a 2022 staff report, the U.S.
segments.tr: 2022년 한 직원 보고서에서 미국

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission described dark patterns as design practices that trick or manipulate people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make.
segments.tr: 연방거래위원회(FTC)는 다크 패턴을 사람들이 원래 하지 않았을 선택을 하도록 속이거나 조종하는 설계 관행으로 설명했습니다.

segments.src: Common types include:
segments.tr: 흔한 유형은 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** Signing up takes one click. Canceling takes a phone call during business hours.
segments.tr: - **로치 모텔:** 가입은 클릭 한 번이면 되지만, 해지는 업무 시간에 전화를 걸어야 합니다.

segments.src: - **Confirmshaming:** The decline button says something like "No thanks, I don't like saving money."
segments.tr: - **죄책감 유발 문구(Confirmshaming):** 거절 버튼에 "아니요, 저는 돈 아끼는 거 싫어요" 같은 문구가 적혀 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** The advertised price grows as you move toward checkout and fees get added.
segments.tr: - **드립 프라이싱:** 결제 단계로 넘어갈수록 광고된 가격이 올라가고, 수수료가 추가됩니다.

segments.src: - **Fake urgency or scarcity:** "Only 2 left!" or a timer that isn't true.
segments.tr: - **가짜 긴박감 또는 희소성:** "2개 남았어요!" 같은 문구나 사실이 아닌 타이머.

segments.src: - **Sneak into basket / pre-checked boxes:** Add-ons you never chose.
segments.tr: - **장바구니 몰래 넣기 / 미리 체크된 상자:** 선택하지 않은 부가 상품이 담겨 있는 경우.

segments.src: The well-being side is about **overconsumption**.
segments.tr: 웰빙 측면은 **과소비**와 관련됩니다.

segments.src: Research on materialism and hedonic adaptation shows that the lift from a new purchase usually fades quickly, and we drift back to our baseline mood.
segments.tr: 물질주의와 쾌락 적응에 관한 연구는 새 물건으로 얻는 기분 상승이 보통 빠르게 사라지고, 우리가 원래의 기분 수준으로 되돌아간다는 것을 보여 줍니다.

segments.src: Easy credit, one-click checkout, and "buy now, pay later" all make spending feel less painful.
segments.tr: 쉬운 신용 대출, 원클릭 결제, "지금 사고 나중에 결제"는 모두 지출의 고통을 줄여 줍니다.

segments.src: That's convenient, but it also makes it easier to spend more than you planned.
segments.tr: 편리하긴 하지만, 계획보다 더 많이 쓰게 만들기도 합니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Maya, a college student in Ohio, signs up for a streaming service's "free 7-day trial."
segments.tr: 오하이오에 사는 대학생 Maya는 한 스트리밍 서비스의 "7일 무료 체험"에 가입합니다.

segments.src: The page asks for a card number "just to verify."
segments.tr: 페이지는 "확인용으로만" 카드 번호를 요구합니다.

segments.src: In small gray text it says the plan renews at $15.99/month.
segments.tr: 작은 회색 글씨로 요금제가 월 $15.99로 자동 갱신된다고 적혀 있습니다.

segments.src: Starting the trial takes one button.
segments.tr: 체험을 시작하는 데는 버튼 하나면 충분합니다.

segments.src: She forgets about it, and three months later she notices $47.97 on her bank statement.
segments.tr: 그녀는 잊어버렸고, 석 달 뒤 은행 명세서에서 $47.97을 발견합니다.

segments.src: When she tries to cancel, she has to go through four screens.
segments.tr: 해지하려고 하자 화면 네 개를 거쳐야 합니다.

segments.src: One says, "Are you sure?
segments.tr: 한 화면에는 "정말요?

segments.src: You'll lose all your saved shows!"
segments.tr: 저장해 둔 모든 쇼를 잃게 됩니다!"

segments.src: (loss aversion), and another offers "50% off for 2 months" (anchoring plus a retention offer).
segments.tr: (손실 회피)라고 적혀 있고, 다른 화면은 "2개월간 50% 할인"을 제안합니다(앵커링 더하기 유지 혜택).

segments.src: The cancel link is pale text under a bright "Keep My Plan" button.
segments.tr: 해지 링크는 밝은 "내 요금제 유지" 버튼 아래 흐릿한 글씨로만 되어 있습니다.

segments.src: None of these tactics is mysterious.
segments.tr: 이 전술들은 전혀 신비로울 것이 없습니다.

segments.src: Each one is a concept from this course: defaults, inattention, loss aversion, anchoring, and visual salience.
segments.tr: 각각은 이 강의에서 다룬 개념입니다. 기본값, 무관심, 손실 회피, 앵커링, 시각적 두드러짐이죠.

segments.src: An ethical version would use the same psychology to help her.
segments.tr: 윤리적인 버전은 같은 심리를 그녀를 돕는 데 씁니다.

segments.src: It would send an email reminder before the trial ends, label the price clearly, and offer one-click cancellation.
segments.tr: 체험이 끝나기 전에 알림 이메일을 보내고, 가격을 명확하게 표시하고, 한 번의 클릭으로 해지할 수 있게 해 주는 식입니다.

segments.src: A quick personal check before buying: *Would I still want this if checkout took 24 hours?
segments.tr: 구매 전 간단한 자기 점검: *결제가 24시간 걸린다면 여전히 이것을 원할까?

segments.src: Would I sign up if canceling were as hard as this company makes it?*
segments.tr: 이 회사가 만든 것처럼 해지가 어렵다면 그래도 가입할까?*

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Consumer psychology tools like attention, memory, social proof, and heuristics are neutral. What makes them ethical or not is whether they help or harm the person deciding.
segments.tr: 1. 주의, 기억, 사회적 증거, 휴리스틱 같은 소비자 심리 도구는 그 자체로는 중립적입니다. 이것이 윤리적인지 아닌지는 그 도구가 결정하는 사람을 돕는지 해치는지에 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. Dark patterns such as roach motels, confirmshaming, drip pricing, and fake scarcity exploit predictable biases to get choices people wouldn't make freely.
segments.tr: 2. 로치 모텔, 죄책감 유발 문구, 드립 프라이싱, 가짜 희소성 같은 다크 패턴은 예측 가능한 편향을 이용해 사람들이 자유롭게 하지 않을 선택을 하도록 만듭니다.

segments.src: 3. Purchases give short-lived happiness because of hedonic adaptation, so slowing down and making costs visible protects both your wallet and your well-being.
segments.tr: 3. 구매가 주는 행복은 쾌락 적응 때문에 오래가지 않습니다. 그래서 속도를 늦추고 비용을 눈에 보이게 하면 지갑과 웰빙 모두를 지킬 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Dark pattern:** An interface design that steers users toward choices that benefit the company at the user's expense.
segments.tr: - **다크 패턴:** 사용자의 희생 위에서 회사에 이익이 되는 선택으로 사용자를 유도하는 인터페이스 설계.

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** A setup where getting into something, like a subscription, is easy and getting out is deliberately hard.
segments.tr: - **로치 모텔:** 구독처럼 들어가기는 쉽지만 빠져나오기는 의도적으로 어렵게 만든 구조.

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** Showing a low headline price and revealing mandatory fees bit by bit during checkout.
segments.tr: - **드립 프라이싱:** 낮은 헤드라인 가격을 보여 준 뒤, 결제 과정에서 필수 수수료를 조금씩 드러내는 방식.

segments.src: - **Hedonic adaptation:** The tendency to return to a baseline level of happiness after positive (or negative) changes, including new purchases.
segments.tr: - **쾌락 적응:** 긍정적(또는 부정적) 변화, 새 구매를 포함한 뒤에 행복의 기준선으로 되돌아가려는 경향.

segments.src: - **Choice architecture:** The way options are arranged and presented, which shapes decisions even when no option is removed.
segments.tr: - **선택 설계(Choice architecture):** 선택지가 배열되고 제시되는 방식. 어떤 선택지도 빠지지 않아도 결정을 형성합니다.

segments.src: A default becomes a problem when it's hidden or works against the user's interests.
segments.tr: 기본값은 숨겨져 있거나 사용자의 이익에 반할 때 문제가 됩니다.

segments.src: That's convenient, but it also makes it easier to spend more than you planned.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life

segments.src: Maya, a college student in Ohio, signs up for a streaming service's "free 7-day trial."

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三句话总结

segments.src: 1. Consumer psychology tools like attention, memory, social proof, and heuristics are neutral. What makes them ethical or not is whether they help or harm the person deciding.
segments.tr: 1. 注意力、记忆、社会证明和启发式等消费者心理工具本身是中性的。决定它们是否合乎伦理的，是它们帮助还是伤害了做决定的人。

segments.src: 2. Dark patterns such as roach motels, confirmshaming, drip pricing, and fake scarcity exploit predictable biases to get choices people wouldn't make freely.
segments.tr: 2. 暗黑模式（如蟑螂旅馆、羞辱式文案、滴漏式定价和虚假稀缺）利用可预测的偏差，让人做出他们若能自由选择便不会做出的选择。

segments.src: 3. Purchases give short-lived happiness because of hedonic adaptation, so slowing down and making costs visible protects both your wallet and your well-being.
segments.tr: 3. 由于享乐适应，购物带来的快乐转瞬即逝。因此放慢节奏、让成本清晰可见，既能保护你的钱包，也能保护你的福祉。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Dark pattern:** An interface design that steers users toward choices that benefit the company at the user's expense.
segments.tr: - **暗黑模式：** 一种界面设计，引导用户做出以公司利益为先、以用户利益为代价的选择。

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** A setup where getting into something, like a subscription, is easy and getting out is deliberately hard.
segments.tr: - **蟑螂旅馆：** 一种设置，使人很容易进入某种状态（如订阅），却刻意让人很难退出。

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** Showing a low headline price and revealing mandatory fees bit by bit during checkout.
segments.tr: - **滴漏式定价：** 先展示较低的标价，然后在结账过程中一点点披露必须支付的费用。

segments.src: - **Hedonic adaptation:** The tendency to return to a baseline level of happiness after positive (or negative) changes, including new purchases.
segments.tr: - **享乐适应：** 在积极（或消极）变化之后，人们倾向于回到原有快乐水平的趋势，包括新购买带来的变化。

segments.src: - **Choice architecture:** The way options are arranged and presented, which shapes decisions even when no option is removed.
segments.tr: - **选择架构：** 选项的排列与呈现方式，即使没有删除任何选项，也会影响决策。

segments.src: Defaults are unavoidable in design, and they can be helpful, like automatic retirement-plan enrollment with an easy opt-out.

segments.src: A default becomes a problem when it's hidden or works against the user's interests.
segments.tr: 只有当默认选项被隐藏或与用户利益相悖时，才会成为问题。

segments.src: > The psychology that makes marketing work, like attention, memory, and mental shortcuts, can help people choose well or push them into choices they regret. Ethics comes down to which of those two things a design is doing.
segments.tr: > वे मनोवैज्ञानिक तरीके जो मार्केटिंग को कारगर बनाते हैं, जैसे ध्यान, स्मृति और मानसिक शॉर्टकट, लोगों को सोच-समझकर चुनाव करने में मदद कर सकते हैं, या उन्हें ऐसे फ़ैसलों की ओर धकेल सकते हैं जिन पर उन्हें बाद में पछतावा हो। नैतिकता का सवाल इस पर आता है कि कोई डिज़ाइन इनमें से कौन-सा काम कर रहा है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: इस श्रृंखला में हमने देखा है कि उपभोक्ता चीज़ों पर कैसे ध्यान देते हैं, उन्हें कैसे याद रखते हैं, उनके रवैये कैसे बनते हैं, सामाजिक दबाव के आगे वे कैसे झुकते हैं, और वे मानसिक शॉर्टकट कैसे अपनाते हैं।

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: यहाँ संक्षिप्त सार है:

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **धारणा और ध्यान:** हम अपने आसपास की बहुत थोड़ी चीज़ों पर ही ध्यान देते हैं, इसलिए तुलना, गति और नवीनता हमारा ध्यान खींचती हैं।

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **स्मृति:** जिन ब्रांड्स को हमने कई बार देखा है वे परिचित लगते हैं, और जो चीज़ें परिचित लगती हैं वे सुरक्षित भी लगती हैं।

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **रवैये और मनाना:** जब हम किसी चीज़ की परवाह करते हैं और हमारे पास समय होता है, तो मज़बूत तर्क हमें मनाते हैं। जब हमारा ध्यान बँटा होता है, तो किसी मशहूर चेहरे, याद रह जाने वाली धुन या बड़े आँकड़े जैसे सतही संकेत काम कर जाते हैं।

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **सामाजिक प्रभाव:** समीक्षाएँ, "बेस्टसेलर" बैज और हमारे दोस्त क्या खरीद रहे हैं, ये सब बताते हैं कि क्या सामान्य है।

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **फ़ैसले के शॉर्टकट (ह्यूरिस्टिक्स):** एंकरिंग, हानि से बचाव, डिफ़ॉल्ट विकल्प और कमी का एहसास हमें जल्दी फ़ैसला लेने में मदद करते हैं, और इनका दुरुपयोग करना भी आसान है।

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: इन सभी उपकरणों का इस्तेमाल दो तरह से किया जा सकता है।

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: कीमतों की तुलना में मदद करने वाला साफ़ लेबल ध्यान का ईमानदार इस्तेमाल है।

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: हर बार पेज रीलोड करने पर फिर से शुरू होने वाला काउंटडाउन टाइमर उसी उपकरण का इस्तेमाल करके आपको धोखा देता है।

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: जब कोई डिज़ाइन जानबूझकर उपयोगकर्ता के अपने हितों के खिलाफ काम करता है, तो उसे **डार्क पैटर्न** कहा जाता है।

segments.src: In a 2022 staff report, the U.S.
segments.tr: 2022 की एक स्टाफ़ रिपोर्ट में, अमेरिका के

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission described dark patterns as design practices that trick or manipulate people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make.
segments.tr: फ़ेडरल ट्रेड कमीशन ने डार्क पैटर्न को उन डिज़ाइन प्रथाओं के रूप में वर्णित किया है जो लोगों को ऐसे फ़ैसलों में फँसाती या प्रभावित करती हैं जो वे अन्यथा नहीं लेते।

segments.src: Common types include:
segments.tr: इनके आम प्रकार हैं:

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** Signing up takes one click. Canceling takes a phone call during business hours.
segments.tr: - **रोच मोटल:** साइन-अप करने में एक क्लिक लगता है। रद्द करने के लिए कार्य-समय में फ़ोन कॉल करना पड़ता है।

segments.tr: - **कन्फ़र्मशेमिंग:** इनकार वाले बटन पर लिखा होता है, "नहीं धन्यवाद, मुझे पैसे बचाना पसंद नहीं है।"

segments.tr: - **ड्रिप प्राइसिंग:** चेकआउट की ओर बढ़ते हुए विज्ञापित कीमत बढ़ती जाती है, और शुल्क जुड़ते जाते हैं।

segments.tr: - **नकली तात्कालिकता या कमी:** "केवल 2 बचे हैं!" या ऐसा टाइमर जो सच नहीं है।

segments.tr: - **चुपके से टोकरी में डालना / पहले से चिह्नित बॉक्स:** ऐसे अतिरिक्त सामान जो आपने कभी चुने ही नहीं।

segments.src: The well-being side is about **overconsumption**.
segments.tr: उपभोक्तावाद के कल्याण-पक्ष का संबंध **अत्यधिक उपभोग** से है।

segments.src: Research on materialism and hedonic adaptation shows that the lift from a new purchase usually fades quickly, and we drift back to our baseline mood.
segments.tr: भौतिकवाद और हेडोनिक एडैप्टेशन पर हुए शोध बताते हैं कि नई खरीद से मिलने वाली खुशी आमतौर पर जल्दी फीकी पड़ जाती है, और हम अपने सामान्य मनोभाव पर लौट आते हैं।

es.title: Las mismas tácticas que venden también pueden atrapar: ética, bienestar y un repaso completo del curso

segments.src: > The psychology that makes marketing work, like attention, memory, and mental shortcuts, can help people choose well or push them into choices they regret. Ethics comes down to which of those two things a design is doing.
segments.tr: > La psicología que hace funcionar el marketing, como la atención, la memoria y los atajos mentales, puede ayudar a elegir bien o empujar a decisiones de las que luego uno se arrepiente. La ética depende de cuál de esas dos cosas hace el diseño.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: A lo largo de esta serie hemos visto cómo los consumidores notan las cosas, las recuerdan, forman actitudes, ceden a la presión social y usan atajos mentales.

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: Esta es la versión corta:

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **Percepción y atención:** Solo notamos una pequeña parte de lo que nos rodea, así que el contraste, el movimiento y la novedad captan nuestra atención.

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **Memoria:** Las marcas que hemos visto muchas veces nos resultan familiares, y lo familiar tiende a parecer seguro.

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **Actitudes y persuasión:** Cuando nos importa algo y tenemos tiempo, nos persuaden los argumentos sólidos. Cuando estamos distraídos, hacen el trabajo las señales superficiales, como una celebridad, una melodía pegadiza o una cifra grande.

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **Influencia social:** Las reseñas, las insignias de «más vendido» y lo que compran nuestros amigos indican qué es lo normal.

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **Atajos de decisión (heurísticos):** El anclaje, la aversión a la pérdida, las opciones predeterminadas y la escasez nos ayudan a decidir rápido, y también son fáciles de explotar.

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: Cada una de estas herramientas puede usarse de dos maneras.

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: Una etiqueta clara que ayuda a comparar precios usa la atención de forma honesta.

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: Un temporizador de cuenta regresiva que se reinicia cada vez que recargas la página usa la misma herramienta para engañarte.

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: Cuando un diseño trabaja deliberadamente contra los intereses del propio usuario, se llama **patrón oscuro**.

segments.src: In a 2022 staff report, the U.S.
segments.tr: En un informe del personal de 2022, la

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission described dark patterns as design practices that trick or manipulate people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make.
segments.tr: Comisión Federal de Comercio de EE. UU. describió los patrones oscuros como prácticas de diseño que engañan o manipulan a las personas para que tomen decisiones que, de otro modo, no tomarían.

segments.src: Common types include:
segments.tr: Los tipos más comunes incluyen:

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** Signing up takes one click. Canceling takes a phone call during business hours.
segments.tr: - **Motel de cucarachas:** Suscribirse cuesta un clic. Cancelar requiere una llamada telefónica en horario laboral.

segments.src: - **Confirmshaming:** The decline button says something like "No thanks, I don't like saving money."
segments.tr: - **Culpabilización forzada (confirmshaming):** El botón de rechazo dice algo como «No, gracias, no me gusta ahorrar dinero».

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** The advertised price grows as you move toward checkout and fees get added.
segments.tr: - **Precios por goteo:** El precio anunciado aumenta a medida que avanzas hacia el pago y se añaden tarifas.

segments.src: - **Fake urgency or scarcity:** "Only 2 left!" or a timer that isn't true.
segments.tr: - **Urgencia o escasez falsas:** «¡Solo quedan 2!» o un temporizador que no es real.

segments.src: - **Sneak into basket / pre-checked boxes:** Add-ons you never chose.
segments.tr: - **Colar en la cesta / casillas preseleccionadas:** Complementos que nunca elegiste.

segments.src: The well-being side is about **overconsumption**.
segments.tr: El lado del bienestar tiene que ver con el **consumo excesivo**.

segments.src: Research on materialism and hedonic adaptation shows that the lift from a new purchase usually fades quickly, and we drift back to our baseline mood.
segments.tr: La investigación sobre el materialismo y la adaptación hedónica muestra que la subida de ánimo que produce una compra nueva suele desvanecerse rápido, y volvemos a nuestro estado de ánimo habitual.

segments.src: Easy credit, one-click checkout, and "buy now, pay later" all make spending feel less painful.
segments.tr: El crédito fácil, el pago con un clic y «compra ahora, paga después» hacen que gastar resulte menos doloroso.

segments.src: That's convenient, but it also makes it easier to spend more than you planned.
segments.tr: Eso es cómodo, pero también facilita gastar más de lo que planeabas.

segments.tr: > علم النفس الذي يجعل التسويق فعّالاً، كالانتباه والذاكرة والاختصارات الذهنية، يمكن أن يساعد الناس على الاختيار الجيد، ويمكن أن يدفعهم أيضاً إلى قرارات يندمون عليها. وتتوقف الأخلاقية على أي هذين الأمرين يفعله التصميم.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: على مدى هذه السلسلة تناولنا كيف يلاحظ المستهلكون الأشياء، ويتذكرونها، ويكوّنون المواقف، ويرضخون للضغط الاجتماعي، ويلجؤون إلى الاختصارات الذهنية.

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: إليك الخلاصة المختصرة:

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **الإدراك والانتباه:** لا نلاحظ إلا جزءاً صغيراً مما حولنا، لذلك تجذب التباينات والحركة والجِدّة انتباهنا.

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **الذاكرة:** العلامات التجارية التي رأيناها مراراً تبدو مألوفة، والأشياء المألوفة تميل إلى أن تبدو آمنة.

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **المواقف والإقناع:** حين نهتم ولدينا وقت، نقتنع بالحجج القوية. وحين نكون مشتّتين، تقوم مؤشرات سطحية مثل المشهور أو اللحن الجذاب أو الرقم الكبير بالعمل نيابةً عنها.

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **التأثير الاجتماعي:** المراجعات وشارات «الأكثر مبيعاً» وما يشتريه أصدقاؤنا كلها تشير إلى ما هو «طبيعي».

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **اختصارات القرار (الاستدلالات):** التثبيت على مرجع، وكراهية الخسارة، والخيارات الافتراضية، والندرة تساعدنا على القرار بسرعة، وهي في الوقت نفسه سهلة الاستغلال.

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: كل واحدة من هذه الأدوات يمكن استخدامها بطريقتين.

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: ملصق واضح يساعدك على مقارنة الأسعار يستخدم الانتباه بأمانة.

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: أما عداد تنازلي يُعاد ضبطه كلما أعدت تحميل الصفحة فيستخدم الأداة نفسها لخداعك.

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: حين يعمل التصميم عمداً ضد مصلحة المستخدم، يُسمّى ذلك **نمطاً مظلماً**.

segments.src: In a 2022 staff report, the U.S.
segments.tr: في تقرير للموظفين صدر عام 2022،

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission described dark patterns as design practices that trick or manipulate people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make.
segments.tr: وصفت لجنة التجارة الفيدرالية الأمريكية الأنماط المظلمة بأنها ممارسات تصميم تخدع الناس أو تتلاعب بهم ليتخذوا قرارات ما كانوا ليتخذوها لولا ذلك.

segments.src: Common types include:
segments.tr: ومن أنواعها الشائعة:

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** Signing up takes one click. Canceling takes a phone call during business hours.
segments.tr: - **فندق الصراصير (Roach motel):** الاشتراك يتطلب نقرة واحدة، أما الإلغاء فيتطلب مكالمة هاتفية خلال ساعات الدوام.

segments.src: - **Confirmshaming:** The decline button says something like "No thanks, I don't like saving money."
segments.tr: - **الإحراج القسري (Confirmshaming):** يقول زر الرفض شيئاً مثل «لا شكراً، أنا لا أحب توفير المال».

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** The advertised price grows as you move toward checkout and fees get added.
segments.tr: - **التسعير التدريجي (Drip pricing):** يرتفع السعر المعلن كلما تقدمت نحو الدفع وأُضيفت الرسوم.

segments.src: - **Fake urgency or scarcity:** "Only 2 left!" or a timer that isn't true.
segments.tr: - **الاستعجال أو الندرة المزيفة:** «بقي 2 فقط!» أو عداد زمني غير حقيقي.

segments.src: - **Sneak into basket / pre-checked boxes:** Add-ons you never chose.
segments.tr: - **الإضافة خفيةً إلى السلة / المربعات المحددة مسبقاً:** إضافات لم تختَرها أنت.

segments.src: The well-being side is about **overconsumption**.
segments.tr: الجانب المتعلق بالرفاهية هو **الإفراط في الاستهلاك**.

segments.src: Research on materialism and hedonic adaptation shows that the lift from a new purchase usually fades quickly, and we drift back to our baseline mood.
segments.tr: تُظهر الأبحاث حول النزعة المادية والتكيّف الهيدوني أن الارتياح الذي يمنحه الشراء الجديد يتلاشى عادةً بسرعة، ونعود إلى مزاجنا المعتاد.

segments.src: Easy credit, one-click checkout, and "buy now, pay later" all make spending feel less painful.
segments.tr: القروض السهلة والدفع بنقرة واحدة و«اشترِ الآن وادفع لاحقاً» كلها تجعل الإنفاق يبدو أقل إيلاماً.

segments.src: That's convenient, but it also makes it easier to spend more than you planned.
segments.tr: هذا مريح، لكنه يجعل إنفاق أكثر مما خططت له أسهل.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Maya, a college student in Ohio, signs up for a streaming service's "free 7-day trial."
segments.tr: مايا، طالبة جامعية في ولاية أوهايو، تشترك في «تجربة مجانية لمدة 7 أيام» لخدمة بث.

segments.tr: تطلب الصفحة رقم بطاقة «فقط للتحقق».

segments.src: In small gray text it says the plan renews at $15.99/month.
segments.tr: وفي نص رمادي صغير مكتوب أن الخطة تُجدَّد بمبلغ 15.99 دولاراً شهرياً.

segments.src: Starting the trial takes one button.
segments.tr: بدء التجربة يتطلب زراً واحداً.

segments.src: She forgets about it, and three months later she notices $47.97 on her bank statement.
segments.tr: تنسى الأمر، وبعد ثلاثة أشهر تلاحظ مبلغ 47.97 دولاراً في كشف حسابها البنكي.

segments.src: When she tries to cancel, she has to go through four screens.
segments.tr: حين تحاول الإلغاء، عليها أن تمر بأربع شاشات.

segments.src: One says, "Are you sure?
segments.tr: تقول إحداها: «هل أنت متأكد؟

segments.src: You'll lose all your saved shows!"
segments.tr: ستفقد جميع العروض التي حفظتها!»

segments.src: (loss aversion), and another offers "50% off for 2 months" (anchoring plus a retention offer).
segments.tr: (كراهية الخسارة)، وتعرض أخرى «خصم 50% لمدة شهرين» (تثبيت على مرجع مع عرض للاحتفاظ بالعميل).

segments.src: The cancel link is pale text under a bright "Keep My Plan" button.
segments.tr: أما رابط الإلغاء فنص باهت تحت زر ساطع اسمه «احتفظ بخطتي».

segments.src: None of these tactics is mysterious.
segments.tr: لا شيء من هذه الأساليب غامض.

segments.src: Each one is a concept from this course: defaults, inattention, loss aversion, anchoring, and visual salience.
segments.tr: كل واحد منها مفهوم من هذا المقرر: الخيارات الافتراضية، وعدم الانتباه، وكراهية الخسارة، والتثبيت على مرجع، والبروز البصري.

segments.src: An ethical version would use the same psychology to help her.
segments.tr: النسخة الأخلاقية ستستخدم علم النفس نفسه لمساعدتها.

segments.src: It would send an email reminder before the trial ends, label the price clearly, and offer one-click cancellation.
segments.tr: ستُرسل تذكيراً بالبريد الإلكتروني قبل انتهاء التجربة، وتوضح السعر بجلاء، وتتيح الإلغاء بنقرة واحدة.

segments.src: A quick personal check before buying: *Would I still want this if checkout took 24 hours?
segments.tr: فحص شخصي سريع قبل الشراء: *هل ما زلت أريد هذا لو استغرق الدفع 24 ساعة؟

segments.src: Would I sign up if canceling were as hard as this company makes it?*

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Consumer psychology tools like attention, memory, social proof, and heuristics are neutral. What makes them ethical or not is whether they help or harm the person deciding.
segments.tr: 1. أدوات علم النفس الاستهلاكي، كالانتباه والذاكرة والدليل الاجتماعي والاختصارات الذهنية، محايدة. ما يجعلها أخلاقية أو غير أخلاقية هو هل تساعد الشخص الذي يتخذ القرار أم تضره.

segments.src: 2. Dark patterns such as roach motels, confirmshaming, drip pricing, and fake scarcity exploit predictable biases to get choices people wouldn't make freely.
segments.tr: 2. الأنماط المظلمة، مثل فندق الصراصير والإحراج القسري والتسعير التدريجي والندرة المزيفة، تستغل تحيزات يمكن التنبؤ بها لتحقيق اختيارات ما كان الناس ليتخذونها بحرية.

segments.src: 3. Purchases give short-lived happiness because of hedonic adaptation, so slowing down and making costs visible protects both your wallet and your well-being.
segments.tr: 3. تمنح المشتريات سعادة قصيرة الأمد بسبب التكيّف الهيدوني، لذلك فإن التمهّل وإظهار التكاليف بوضوح يحميان محفظتك ورفاهيتك معاً.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms

segments.src: - **Dark pattern:** An interface design that steers users toward choices that benefit the company at the user's expense.
segments.tr: - **النمط المظلم:** تصميم واجهة يوجّه المستخدمين نحو خيارات تفيد الشركة على حساب المستخدم.

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** A setup where getting into something, like a subscription, is easy and getting out is deliberately hard.
segments.tr: - **فندق الصراصير:** إعداد يكون فيه الدخول إلى شيء، كاشتراك، سهلاً، بينما الخروج منه صعب عمداً.

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** Showing a low headline price and revealing mandatory fees bit by bit during checkout.
segments.tr: - **التسعير التدريجي:** عرض سعر أولي منخفض، ثم الكشف عن الرسوم الإلزامية تدريجياً أثناء الدفع.

segments.src: - **Hedonic adaptation:** The tendency to return to a baseline level of happiness after positive (or negative) changes, including new purchases.
segments.tr: - **التكيّف الهيدوني:** الميل إلى العودة إلى مستوى السعادة الأساسي بعد التغيّرات الإيجابية (أو السلبية)، بما في ذلك المشتريات الجديدة.

segments.src: - **Choice architecture:** The way options are arranged and presented, which shapes decisions even when no option is removed.

pt.title: [Psicologia do Consumidor #15] As mesmas táticas que vendem também podem prender: ética, bem-estar e uma recapitulação completa do curso

segments.src: > The psychology that makes marketing work, like attention, memory, and mental shortcuts, can help people choose well or push them into choices they regret. Ethics comes down to which of those two things a design is doing.
segments.tr: > A psicologia que faz o marketing funcionar, como atenção, memória e atalhos mentais, pode ajudar as pessoas a escolher bem ou empurrá-las para escolhas de que se arrependem. A ética se resume a qual dessas duas coisas um design está fazendo.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: Ao longo desta série, vimos como os consumidores percebem coisas, lembram delas, formam atitudes, cedem à pressão social e usam atalhos mentais.

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: Aqui está a versão resumida:

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **Percepção e atenção:** Só notamos uma pequena parte do que está ao nosso redor, então contraste, movimento e novidade chamam nossa atenção.

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **Memória:** Marcas que já vimos muitas vezes parecem familiares, e o que parece familiar tende a parecer seguro.

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **Atitudes e persuasão:** Quando nos importamos e temos tempo, somos persuadidos por argumentos fortes. Quando estamos distraídos, sinais superficiais como uma celebridade, um jingle chiclete ou um número grande fazem o trabalho.

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **Influência social:** Avaliações, selos de "mais vendido" e o que nossos amigos compram sinalizam o que é normal.

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **Atalhos de decisão (heurísticas):** Ancoragem, aversão à perda, opções padrão e escassez nos ajudam a decidir rapidamente, e também são fáceis de explorar.

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: Cada uma dessas ferramentas pode ser usada de duas formas.

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: Um rótulo claro que ajuda você a comparar preços usa a atenção de forma honesta.

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: Um cronômetro de contagem regressiva que se reinicia toda vez que você recarrega a página usa a mesma ferramenta para enganar você.

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: Quando um design funciona deliberadamente contra os interesses do próprio usuário, isso se chama **padrão obscuro** (dark pattern).

segments.src: In a 2022 staff report, the U.S.
segments.tr: Em um relatório de equipe de 2022, a

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission described dark patterns as design practices that trick or manipulate people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make.
segments.tr: Federal Trade Commission dos EUA descreveu os padrões obscuros como práticas de design que enganam ou manipulam as pessoas para que façam escolhas que não fariam de outra forma.

segments.src: Common types include:
segments.tr: Tipos comuns incluem:

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** Signing up takes one click. Canceling takes a phone call during business hours.
segments.tr: - **Motel da barata (roach motel):** Cadastrar-se leva um clique. Cancelar exige uma ligação em horário comercial.

segments.src: - **Confirmshaming:** The decline button says something like "No thanks, I don't like saving money."
segments.tr: - **Constrangimento por confirmação (confirmshaming):** O botão de recusa diz algo como "Não, obrigado, eu não gosto de economizar dinheiro".

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** The advertised price grows as you move toward checkout and fees get added.
segments.tr: - **Preço gotejante (drip pricing):** O preço anunciado aumenta conforme você avança até o checkout e as taxas são acrescentadas.

segments.src: - **Fake urgency or scarcity:** "Only 2 left!" or a timer that isn't true.
segments.tr: - **Urgência ou escassez falsa:** "Restam só 2!" ou um cronômetro que não é verdadeiro.

segments.src: - **Sneak into basket / pre-checked boxes:** Add-ons you never chose.
segments.tr: - **Entrada sorrateira no carrinho / caixas pré-marcadas:** Complementos que você nunca escolheu.

segments.src: The well-being side is about **overconsumption**.
segments.tr: O lado do bem-estar é sobre **consumo excessivo**.

segments.src: Research on materialism and hedonic adaptation shows that the lift from a new purchase usually fades quickly, and we drift back to our baseline mood.
segments.tr: Pesquisas sobre materialismo e adaptação hedônica mostram que a sensação de prazer de uma nova compra costuma desaparecer rapidamente, e voltamos ao nosso humor de base.

segments.src: Easy credit, one-click checkout, and "buy now, pay later" all make spending feel less painful.
segments.tr: Crédito fácil, checkout com um clique e "compre agora, pague depois" fazem o gasto parecer menos doloroso.

segments.src: > The psychology that makes marketing work, like attention, memory, and mental shortcuts, can help people choose well or push them into choices they regret. Ethics comes down to which of those two things a design is doing.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: このシリーズでは、消費者が物事にどう気づき、どう記憶し、どう態度を形成し、社会的圧力にどう屈し、どう心理的な近道を取るのかを見てきました。

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: 要点をまとめると次のとおりです：

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **知覚と注意:** 私たちは周囲のごく一部にしか気づかないため、対比、動き、新しさが注意を引きます。

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **記憶:** 何度も目にしたブランドは馴染みがあり、馴染みのあるものは安全に感じられる傾向があります。

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **態度と説得:** 関心があり時間に余裕があるときは、強い論拠によって説得されます。注意散漫なときは、有名人、耳に残るジングル、大きな数字といった表層的な手がかりが役割を果たします。

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **社会的影響:** レビュー、「ベストセラー」バッジ、友人が買っているものはすべて、何が「普通」なのかを示すシグナルになります。

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **意思決定の近道（ヒューリスティック）:** アンカリング、損失回避、デフォルト、希少性は素早い判断を助けますが、悪用もされやすいものです。

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: これらの道具はどれも、二通りの使われ方をします。

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: 価格比較に役立つ明確な表示は、注意を誠実に使っています。

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: ページを再読み込みするたびにリセットされるカウントダウンタイマーは、同じ道具を使ってあなたを欺いています。

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: デザインがユーザー自身の利益に意図的に反して働く場合、それは**ダークパターン**と呼ばれます。

de.title: [Konsumentenpsychologie #15] Die gleichen Tricks, die verkaufen, können auch in die Falle locken: Ethik, Wohlbefinden und eine Zusammenfassung des ganzen Kurses

segments.src: > The psychology that makes marketing work, like attention, memory, and mental shortcuts, can help people choose well or push them into choices they regret. Ethics comes down to which of those two things a design is doing.
segments.tr: > Die Psychologie, die Marketing funktionieren lässt – also Aufmerksamkeit, Gedächtnis und mentale Abkürzungen –, kann Menschen helfen, gut zu wählen, oder sie zu Entscheidungen drängen, die sie bereuen. Ethisch ist ein Design daran zu messen, welche dieser beiden Wirkungen es hat.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Over this series we've looked at how consumers notice things, remember them, form attitudes, give in to social pressure, and take mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: In dieser Serie haben wir uns angesehen, wie Konsumenten Dinge wahrnehmen, sich an sie erinnern, Einstellungen bilden, sozialem Druck nachgeben und mentale Abkürzungen nutzen.

segments.src: Here is the short version:
segments.tr: Hier die Kurzfassung:

segments.src: - **Perception and attention:** We only notice a small part of what's around us, so contrast, motion, and novelty get our attention.
segments.tr: - **Wahrnehmung und Aufmerksamkeit:** Wir bemerken nur einen kleinen Teil dessen, was um uns herum ist, daher ziehen Kontrast, Bewegung und Neuheit unsere Aufmerksamkeit auf sich.

segments.src: - **Memory:** Brands we've seen many times feel familiar, and things that feel familiar tend to feel safe.
segments.tr: - **Gedächtnis:** Marken, die wir oft gesehen haben, wirken vertraut, und Vertrautes wirkt tendenziell sicher.

segments.src: - **Attitudes and persuasion:** When we care and have time, we're persuaded by strong arguments. When we're distracted, surface cues like a celebrity, a catchy jingle, or a big number do the work.
segments.tr: - **Einstellungen und Überzeugung:** Wenn es uns wichtig ist und wir Zeit haben, lassen wir uns von starken Argumenten überzeugen. Wenn wir abgelenkt sind, übernehmen oberflächliche Reize wie ein Prominenter, ein eingängiger Jingle oder eine große Zahl die Arbeit.

segments.src: - **Social influence:** Reviews, "bestseller" badges, and what our friends buy all signal what's normal.
segments.tr: - **Soziale Beeinflussung:** Bewertungen, „Bestseller“-Siegel und was unsere Freunde kaufen, signalisieren, was als normal gilt.

segments.src: - **Decision shortcuts (heuristics):** Anchoring, loss aversion, defaults, and scarcity help us decide quickly, and they're also easy to exploit.
segments.tr: - **Entscheidungsabkürzungen (Heuristiken):** Anker, Verlustaversion, Voreinstellungen und Knappheit helfen uns, schnell zu entscheiden, und sie lassen sich auch leicht ausnutzen.

segments.src: Every one of these tools can be used in two ways.
segments.tr: Jedes dieser Werkzeuge lässt sich auf zwei Arten einsetzen.

segments.src: A clear label that helps you compare prices uses attention honestly.
segments.tr: Ein klares Preisetikett, das den Preisvergleich erleichtert, nutzt Aufmerksamkeit ehrlich.

segments.src: A countdown timer that resets every time you reload the page uses the same tool to deceive you.
segments.tr: Ein Countdown-Timer, der sich bei jedem Neuladen der Seite zurücksetzt, nutzt dasselbe Werkzeug, um dich zu täuschen.

segments.src: When a design deliberately works against the user's own interests, it's called a **dark pattern**.
segments.tr: Wenn ein Design gezielt gegen die eigenen Interessen der Nutzer arbeitet, spricht man von einem **Dark Pattern**.

segments.src: In a 2022 staff report, the U.S.
segments.tr: Im Mitarbeiterbericht von 2022 beschrieb die US-amerikanische

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission described dark patterns as design practices that trick or manipulate people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make.
segments.tr: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Dark Patterns als Designpraktiken, die Menschen durch Täuschung oder Manipulation zu Entscheidungen bringen, die sie sonst nicht treffen würden.

segments.src: Common types include:
segments.tr: Typische Formen sind:

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** Signing up takes one click. Canceling takes a phone call during business hours.
segments.tr: - **Roach Motel:** Die Anmeldung dauert einen Klick. Die Kündigung erfordert einen Anruf während der Geschäftszeiten.

segments.src: - **Confirmshaming:** The decline button says something like "No thanks, I don't like saving money."
segments.tr: - **Confirmshaming:** Der Ablehnen-Button lautet etwa „Nein danke, ich spare nicht gern Geld.“

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** The advertised price grows as you move toward checkout and fees get added.
segments.tr: - **Drip Pricing:** Der angezeigte Preis steigt, je weiter man zur Kasse kommt, weil nach und nach Gebühren hinzukommen.

segments.src: - **Fake urgency or scarcity:** "Only 2 left!" or a timer that isn't true.
segments.tr: - **Künstliche Dringlichkeit oder Knappheit:** „Nur noch 2 verfügbar!“ oder ein Timer, der nicht stimmt.

segments.src: - **Sneak into basket / pre-checked boxes:** Add-ons you never chose.
segments.tr: - **Heimliches Hinzufügen in den Warenkorb / vorangekreuzte Kästchen:** Zusatzleistungen, die man nie gewählt hat.

segments.src: The well-being side is about **overconsumption**.
segments.tr: Die Wohlbefindensseite betrifft den **übermäßigen Konsum**.

segments.src: Research on materialism and hedonic adaptation shows that the lift from a new purchase usually fades quickly, and we drift back to our baseline mood.
segments.tr: Forschung zu Materialismus und hedonischer Adaptation zeigt, dass der Kick durch einen neuen Kauf meist schnell verblasst und wir zu unserer üblichen Stimmung zurückkehren.

segments.src: Easy credit, one-click checkout, and "buy now, pay later" all make spending feel less painful.
segments.tr: Einfache Kredite, Ein-Klick-Checkout und „Jetzt kaufen, später zahlen“ machen das Ausgeben weniger schmerzhaft.

segments.src: That's convenient, but it also makes it easier to spend more than you planned.
segments.tr: Das ist bequem, macht es aber auch leichter, mehr auszugeben als geplant.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Maya, a college student in Ohio, signs up for a streaming service's "free 7-day trial."
segments.tr: Maya, eine Studentin in Ohio, meldet sich für die „kostenlose 7-Tage-Testphase“ eines Streamingdienstes an.

segments.src: The page asks for a card number "just to verify."
segments.tr: Die Seite verlangt eine Kartennummer „nur zur Verifizierung“.

segments.src: In small gray text it says the plan renews at $15.99/month.
segments.tr: Im kleinen grauen Text steht, dass sich der Tarif auf $15.99/Monat verlängert.

segments.src: Starting the trial takes one button.
segments.tr: Um die Testphase zu starten, genügt ein Knopfdruck.

segments.src: She forgets about it, and three months later she notices $47.97 on her bank statement.
segments.tr: Sie denkt nicht mehr daran, und drei Monate später entdeckt sie $47.97 auf ihrem Kontoauszug.

segments.src: When she tries to cancel, she has to go through four screens.
segments.tr: Als sie kündigen will, muss sie durch vier Bildschirme.

segments.src: One says, "Are you sure?
segments.tr: Einer fragt: „Sind Sie sicher?

segments.src: You'll lose all your saved shows!"
segments.tr: Sie verlieren alle gespeicherten Serien!“

segments.src: (loss aversion), and another offers "50% off for 2 months" (anchoring plus a retention offer).
segments.tr: (Verlustaversion), und ein anderer bietet „50 % Rabatt für 2 Monate“ an (Ankereffekt plus ein Bindungsangebot).

segments.src: None of these tactics is mysterious.
segments.tr: Keine dieser Taktiken ist geheimnisvoll.

segments.src: Each one is a concept from this course: defaults, inattention, loss aversion, anchoring, and visual salience.
segments.tr: Jede davon ist ein Konzept aus diesem Kurs: Voreinstellungen, Unaufmerksamkeit, Verlustaversion, Anker und visuelle Auffälligkeit.

segments.src: An ethical version would use the same psychology to help her.
segments.tr: Eine ethische Version würde dieselbe Psychologie nutzen, um ihr zu helfen.

segments.src: It would send an email reminder before the trial ends, label the price clearly, and offer one-click cancellation.
segments.tr: Sie würde vor Ende der Testphase eine E-Mail-Erinnerung schicken, den Preis klar kennzeichnen und eine Kündigung mit einem Klick anbieten.

segments.src: A quick personal check before buying: *Would I still want this if checkout took 24 hours?
segments.tr: Eine kurze persönliche Prüfung vor dem Kauf: *Würde ich es immer noch wollen, wenn der Bestellvorgang 24 Stunden dauerte?

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Consumer psychology tools like attention, memory, social proof, and heuristics are neutral. What makes them ethical or not is whether they help or harm the person deciding.
segments.tr: 1. Werkzeuge der Konsumentenpsychologie wie Aufmerksamkeit, Gedächtnis, sozialer Beweis und Heuristiken sind neutral. Ethisch oder nicht entscheidet sich daran, ob sie der entscheidenden Person helfen oder schaden.

segments.src: 2. Dark patterns such as roach motels, confirmshaming, drip pricing, and fake scarcity exploit predictable biases to get choices people wouldn't make freely.
segments.tr: 2. Dark Patterns wie Roach Motels, Confirmshaming, Drip Pricing und künstliche Knappheit nutzen vorhersehbare Verzerrungen aus, um Entscheidungen zu erzwingen, die Menschen sonst nicht frei treffen würden.

segments.src: 3. Purchases give short-lived happiness because of hedonic adaptation, so slowing down and making costs visible protects both your wallet and your well-being.
segments.tr: 3. Käufe bringen nur kurzfristiges Glück, wegen der hedonischen Adaptation. Wer langsamer wird und die Kosten sichtbar macht, schützt daher Geldbeutel und Wohlbefinden.

segments.src: Maya, a college student in Ohio, signs up for a streaming service's "free 7-day trial."
segments.tr: Maya, một sinh viên đại học ở Ohio, đăng ký "dùng thử miễn phí 7 ngày" của một dịch vụ phát trực tuyến.

segments.tr: Bằng chữ xám nhỏ, trang ghi rằng gói sẽ tự gia hạn với giá 15,99 USD/tháng.

segments.src: Starting the trial takes one button.
segments.tr: Bắt đầu dùng thử chỉ cần một nút.

segments.tr: Cô ấy quên mất, và ba tháng sau thấy khoản 47,97 USD trên sao kê ngân hàng.

segments.src: When she tries to cancel, she has to go through four screens.
segments.tr: Khi cố hủy, cô phải đi qua bốn màn hình.

segments.src: One says, "Are you sure?

segments.src: You'll lose all your saved shows!"

segments.tr: (ghét mất mát), và một màn hình khác đưa ra "giảm 50% trong 2 tháng" (neo giá cộng với ưu đãi giữ chân).

segments.src: None of these tactics is mysterious.
segments.tr: Không chiêu nào trong số này là bí ẩn.

segments.src: Each one is a concept from this course: defaults, inattention, loss aversion, anchoring, and visual salience.
segments.tr: Mỗi chiêu là một khái niệm từ khóa học này: mặc định, lơ là chú ý, ghét mất mát, neo giá và độ nổi bật thị giác.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt trong 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Consumer psychology tools like attention, memory, social proof, and heuristics are neutral. What makes them ethical or not is whether they help or harm the person deciding.
segments.tr: 1. Các công cụ tâm lý người tiêu dùng như chú ý, trí nhớ, bằng chứng xã hội và phím tắt tư duy là trung tính. Điều làm chúng có đạo đức hay không là chúng giúp hay hại người đang quyết định.

segments.src: 2. Dark patterns such as roach motels, confirmshaming, drip pricing, and fake scarcity exploit predictable biases to get choices people wouldn't make freely.
segments.tr: 2. Dark pattern như roach motel, confirmshaming, giá nhỏ giọt và khan hiếm giả khai thác các thiên kiến có thể dự đoán để đạt được những lựa chọn mà người ta sẽ không tự do đưa ra.

segments.src: 3. Purchases give short-lived happiness because of hedonic adaptation, so slowing down and making costs visible protects both your wallet and your well-being.
segments.tr: 3. Việc mua sắm mang lại hạnh phúc ngắn ngủi do thích nghi khoái cảm, nên chậm lại và làm cho chi phí hiện rõ sẽ bảo vệ cả ví tiền lẫn hạnh phúc của bạn.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Dark pattern:** An interface design that steers users toward choices that benefit the company at the user's expense.
segments.tr: - **Dark pattern:** Thiết kế giao diện dẫn người dùng đến những lựa chọn có lợi cho công ty với cái giá là người dùng.

segments.src: - **Roach motel:** A setup where getting into something, like a subscription, is easy and getting out is deliberately hard.
segments.tr: - **Roach motel:** Cách thiết lập mà việc tham gia một thứ gì đó, như gói đăng ký, thì dễ còn việc thoát ra thì cố tình khó.

segments.src: - **Drip pricing:** Showing a low headline price and revealing mandatory fees bit by bit during checkout.
segments.tr: - **Drip pricing:** Hiển thị mức giá tiêu đề thấp và tiết lộ các khoản phí bắt buộc từng chút một trong quá trình thanh toán.

segments.src: - **Hedonic adaptation:** The tendency to return to a baseline level of happiness after positive (or negative) changes, including new purchases.
segments.tr: - **Thích nghi khoái cảm (hedonic adaptation):** Xu hướng quay trở lại mức hạnh phúc nền sau những thay đổi tích cực (hoặc tiêu cực), kể cả khi mua món đồ mới.

segments.src: - **Choice architecture:** The way options are arranged and presented, which shapes decisions even when no option is removed.
segments.tr: - **Kiến trúc lựa chọn (choice architecture):** Cách sắp xếp và trình bày các phương án, định hình quyết định ngay cả khi không phương án nào bị loại bỏ.

segments.src: A default becomes a problem when it's hidden or works against the user's interests.
